title: 4DN Falcon Research Method
bodyHtml:
Unlock the Power of Genetic Data with FALCON

FALCON is a sophisticated statistical engine designed to transform complex genetic data into clear, actionable insights. It seamlessly integrates multiple data streams—including summary statistics from GWAS or EWAS, Linkage Disequilibrium (LD), variant annotations, and variant-to-gene (V2G) maps—to calculate a genetic support score for your genes of interest.

An Intelligent and Adaptive Core Model

At its core, FALCON employs a state-of-the-art probabilistic Bayesian model to deliver unparalleled accuracy.

  • Smart Data Handling: The process begins by normalizing the marginal effect sizes from association studies, standardizing the data to ensure fair and accurate comparisons across all genetic variants and traits.
  • Signal from Noise: Using a powerful “spike-and-slab” method, FALCON intelligently distinguishes between the vast majority of variants with no effect (the “spike”) and the small subset with a genuine, trait-relevant impact (the “slab”).
  • Annotation-Driven Insights: When functional annotations are available, FALCON automatically uses them to refine the probability of a variant’s association with a trait. For unannotated variants, it relies on robust global estimates derived from the data’s underlying genetic architecture.
Solving the Variant-to-Gene Challenge

For this specific analysis, FALCON model's variant-to-gene (V2G) linkage was informed exclusively by evidence-based scores derived from enriched chromatin interaction links from human experiments hosted on the 4D Nucleome (4DN) Data Portal. This approach leverages data on the three-dimensional organization of the genome to connect variants to the distant genes they may regulate.

Robust Inference Delivers Confident Results

Under the hood, FALCON is powered by a Gibbs sampling algorithm that learns iteratively from your data. Convergence is confirmed by rigorous checks like the Gelman–Rubin statistic. Final outputs include:

  • Confident Genetic Support Scores: The posterior probability that a gene or variant is associated with a trait.
  • Fine-Mapped Effect Sizes: Precise estimates of a variant’s true effect.
  • Fine-Linked V2G Connections: The most likely gene target for a trait-relevant variant.
Column Descriptions (FALCON Gene)

Phenotype: Identifies the disease, trait, or biological measurement being analyzed (e.g., LDL cholesterol, Alzheimer’s disease).

Probability: The core “genetic support” score representing the posterior probability that the gene is associated with the trait (0–1); values closer to 1 indicate higher confidence.

P-value: Measures statistical significance; lower values indicate stronger evidence against random chance.

Beta (Effect Size): Estimated magnitude and direction of the gene’s effect (calculated via a heuristic similar to burden methods). Positive values suggest an increase in the trait; negative values suggest a decrease. Larger absolute values imply stronger impact.

Standard Error: Quantifies the precision of the Beta estimate; smaller values indicate more precise, reliable estimates.

V2G Link Score: Provides access to detailed evidence linking variants to the gene. FALCON calculates a posterior probability for these links; showing details reveals the variants driving the association and the model’s confidence for each variant-to-gene connection.

Column Descriptions (V2G Link Score)

Variant ID: Precise genomic location formatted as chromosome:position:reference_allele:alternative_allele.

rsID: The dbSNP Reference SNP ID (rsID), a unique and stable identifier for the variant.

Link probability: The Posterior Linkage Probability calculated by FALCON (0–1), quantifying confidence that a specific variant is functionally linked to the gene. Higher values indicate a stronger, more confident link and are central to FALCON’s “fine-linking” capabilities.
